name: Question 11
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14046771/assets/33e48fa5bdbb034bcf489e038ccf80fc5f67baabeccacc1b7abd741183ebf05d.png)

Consider the square region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)),
$$

where 

$$
x=\frac{v-1}{u+1},\,y=(u+v-1)^{2}+1.
$$

Which of the following is the image of the side ${S}_{4}$ under the action of $T?$
worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the side ${S}_{4}.$

For the side ${S}_{4},$ we have $u=0$ and $1\ge v\ge 0.$ Substituting $u=0$ into our transformation equations, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =(\frac{v-1}{u+1},\,(u+v-1)^{2}+1) \\  & =(\frac{v-1}{0+1},\,(0+v-1)^{2}+1) \\  & =(v-1,\,(v-1)^{2}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the image of ${S}_{4}$ can be parametrized by

$$
x=v-1,\,y=(v-1)^{2}+1,\,1\ge v\ge 0.
$$

 

Writing this in the usual notation, we have

$$
x=t-1,\,y=(t-1)^{2}+1,\,1\ge t\ge 0.
$$

These are parametric equations of a parabolic arc. Notice that if we eliminate $t$ from the equations, we get

$$
y={x}^{2}+1
$$

which is an upward-opening parabola whose vertex is at $(0,1).$

Moreover, the endpoints of ${S}_{4}$ are mapped to the $xy$-plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & T:(0,1)\to (\frac{1-1}{0+1},(0+1-1)^{2}+1)=(0,1) \\  & T:(0,0)\to (\frac{0-1}{0+1},(0+0-1)^{2}+1)=(-1,2)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the image of ${S}_{4}$ is an arc of a upward-opening parabola, traversed from $(0,1)$ to $(-1,2).$

Question 11
?

Consider the square region Δ in the uv-plane, given by Δ={(u,v):0≤u≤1,0≤v≤1},

and the transformation T, given by T:(u,v)→(x(u,v),y(u,v)), where x=v−1u+1,y=(u+v−1)2+1.

Which of the following is the image of the side S4 under the action of T?

a
An arc of a right-opening parabola, traversed from (0,1) to (−1,2).
b
An arc of a right-opening parabola, traversed from (1,1) to (0,2).
c
An arc of an upward-opening parabola, traversed from (−1,2) to (0,1).
d
An arc of a upward-opening parabola, traversed from (0,2) to (1,1).
e
An arc of an upward-opening parabola, traversed from (0,1) to (−1,2).
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To map the entire region Δ onto the xy-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the side S4.

For the side S4, we have u=0 and 1≥v≥0. Substituting u=0 into our transformation equations, we obtain (x,y)=T(u,v)=(v−1u+1,(u+v−1)2+1)=(v−10+1,(0+v−1)2+1)=(v−1,(v−1)2+1).

So, the image of S4 can be parametrized by x=v−1,y=(v−1)2+1,1≥v≥0.

Writing this in the usual notation, we have x=t−1,y=(t−1)2+1,1≥t≥0.

These are parametric equations of a parabolic arc. Notice that if we eliminate t from the equations, we get y=x2+1 which is an upward-opening parabola whose vertex is at (0,1).

Moreover, the endpoints of S4 are mapped to the xy-plane as follows:

T:(0,1)→(1−10+1,(0+1−1)2+1)=(0,1)T:(0,0)→(0−10+1,(0+0−1)2+1)=(−1,2)

Therefore, the image of S4 is an arc of a upward-opening parabola, traversed from (0,1) to (−1,2).
